business_scope.primary_industry_name: Commercial Shipbuilding of Deep-Sea Dry Cargo and Container Vessels

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid – Civil Law commercial codes influenced by Islamic Sharia principles, with codified Companies Law, Anti-Money Laundering Law, and modern regulatory practice
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Oman–United Kingdom Double Taxation Agreement – DTAA (1998)
Oman–France Investment Protection and Promotion Agreement
Oman–US Trade and Investment Framework Agreement (TIFA)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Royal Decree No. 30/2016 Promulgating the Law on Combating Money Laundering and Combating the Financing of Terrorism, as amended and updated by subsequent Sultani Decrees; Executive Regulations of the AML/CFT Law issued by the Central Bank of Oman and the Commercial Companies Law Royal Decree No. 18/2019 (Articles requiring beneficial owner identification and disclosure); Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Investment Promotion (MOCIIP) registrations and Oman Financial Intelligence Unit (OmanFIU) directives; Commercial Registration and Investment Promotion Law framework.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized and certified copy of founder's valid passport
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National Passport Authority / Notary Public in country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Corporate Extract of corporate shareholder (if shareholder is a legal entity)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry in the shareholder's home jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Memorandum of Association and Articles of Association in Arabic (draft executed before notary)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Certified law office / licensed notary in Oman, endorsed by the commercial registry

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Special or General Power of Attorney for corporate formation signatory (if non-resident founder cannot attend in Oman)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate board / corporate secretary in home jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter / professional introduction letter in English or Arabic
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Not required as apostille; submitted as certified original to registered agent or bank

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence on all shareholders, directors, and ultimate beneficial owners using domestic OmanFIU watchlists, OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, UN Security Council consolidated sanctions lists, EU restrictive measures, and Interpol Red Notice checks. The forming agent or registered office provider must retain documentary proof of screening and immediately escalate to the Oman Financial Intelligence Unit where a positive PEP match or sanctions red flag arises. Additional adverse media, multi-jurisdictional ownership tracing, and source-of-funds verification are required for a Single Person Company established for commercial shipbuilding and vessel repair operations.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Invest Easy (Online Investor Services Portal of the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Investment Promotion – MOCIIP) – https://www.investeasy.gov.om
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The primary corporate name shall be in Arabic. The foreign or English transliteration must be a phonetic equivalent which does not distort the meaning, must not conflict with previously registered Arabic names, and must follow the Commercial Registry transliteration conventions. The name suffix 'SPC' (Single Person Company) or 'LLC' equivalent must be represented in Arabic as 'شخص واحد' / 'شركة ذات مسئولية محدودة'. The transliterated English form shall be recorded as supplementary to the Arabic primary name.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Any word implying public agency, religeous authority, or monopoly that has not been licensed with the respective regulator
Any name identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered mark or company
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the requested name is rejected, the applicant or its licensed attorney may file an administrative appeal with the Registration Office of the Directorate General of Commerce at MOCIIP within 30 days of the rejection. The appeal must be submitted via the Invest Easy portal or in written petition with supporting trademark certificate, authorization, and explanation. If the name conflict arises from an objection, the appellant may also oppose the conflicting name through the Commercial Registry grievance procedure. In case of persistent rejection, a fresh name application can be filed and, if necessary, a judicial review action may be initiated before the Administrative Court in Oman.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office is not permissible for a commercial shipyard / manufacturing company registered under ISIC 3011 requiring a physical production site. For the purpose of company law and commercial registration, a registered office address in Oman is mandatory; it may initially be a licensed registered agent address only during the pre-operational hold, but the company must secure a real physical leased/owned industrial plot (shipyard, shed, or slipway) before the construction license, tax registration, and labor permits are issued. Virtual office arrangements will not satisfy the commercial substance and economic presence test for the actual shipyard activity.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High. Oman routinely conducts unannounced commercial and operational inspections for industrial shipbuilding facilities, including visits by the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Investment Promotion, the Ministry of Energy and Minerals, Public Authority for Social Insurance, and the Oman Chamber of Commerce. Quantified risk: greater than 80% probability of an on-site physical inspection within the first 12 months of obtaining the operational license, with follow-up inspections triggered by tax declaration, labor quota utilization, and environmental compliance.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office / registered agent arrangement (first year address provision and statutory filing mailbox)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing Omani corporate services market benchmark, institutional annual fee for registered office and correspondence handling

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/KYC UBO verification and PEP/Sanctions screening packages for individual and corporate UBOs
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: AML compliance service provider / licensed registered agent
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark per issued UBO registry report; includes OFAC, UN, EU, and domestic OmanFIU screening

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Licensed law office fee for preparation of incorporation documents, bilingual MOA, Commercial Registration Form, and ancillary legal advice

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Companies Law of the Sultanate of Oman, Royal Decree No. 18/2019 as amended by Royal Decree No. 92/2020, particularly Articles 87-90 on Single Person Companies, Articles 16-17 on registered office, Articles 59-68 on Commercial Register and publication, and the enabling Executive Regulations; Foreign Capital Investment Law, Royal Decree No. 50/2019, Article 3 and its negative-list provisions permitting 100% foreign ownership of shipbuilding subject to MoCIIP clearance.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Investment Promotion (MoCIIP), Directorate General of Commerce, Commercial Registration Department, operating through the Invest Oman / Oman Business Portal one-stop shop.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum of Association of the Single Person Company (SPC) in Arabic, duly notarized before the Oman Notary Public, filed electronically for issuance of the Commercial Register (CR) extract and followed by statutory publication in the Official Gazette (Al-Jarida Al-Rasmiya).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutorily fixed minimum paid-up capital is prescribed for an SPC under RD 18/2019 as amended; the full subscribed capital stated in the notarized Memorandum of Association must be remitted by the sole shareholder after CR issuance into the company's bank account at a CBO-licensed bank and evidenced by a capital-deposit balance certificate. Funds remitted from abroad must satisfy Central Bank of Oman source-of-funds and balance-of-payments reporting. Customer-advance escrow accounts and Maritime Installment LC structures may be established as commercial payment rails but cannot substitute for or offset the share-capital deposit obligation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED on this date: (i) the sole shareholder subscribes in full to the paid-up capital stated in the Memorandum of Association, to be remitted to the company's bank account and evidenced by a capital-deposit certificate; (ii) the registered office stated in the Memorandum is adopted as the statutory seat, subject to later registered changes; (iii) [Name] and [Name] are appointed Managing Director and Secretary, or a single manager as permitted for an SPC, with authority to open bank accounts, negotiate maritime instalment letters of credit and escrow arrangements, and bind the Company; (iv) an independent auditor is appointed; (v) officers are authorized to execute statutory, industrial, environmental and Civil Defense filings; (vi) all prior incorporation acts are ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: MoCIIP Commercial Registration Department via the Invest Oman business e-portal (one-stop shop).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Login to the MoCIIP business portal and reserve up to three Arabic/Latin trade names; select the Single Person Company entity type and the ISIC 3011 / NAICS 336611 shipbuilding scope; enter the sole shareholder beneficial-ownership declaration; the system runs a name-collision check and an AML/sanctions screen against ROP and Central Bank of Oman watchlists; upload passport copies and a capital-block declaration.
required_dossiers: Shareholder passport or Omani National ID
Arabic and Latin trade name reservation form
Beneficial ownership and AML declaration
Projected activity matrix under ISIC 3011
Proposed registered office address sketch
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name conflicts with an existing Commercial Register entry or a prohibited word, file a written reconsideration with the MoCIIP name committee together with two alternative names within 10 business days. If the shipbuilding activity is flagged for sector policy review, submit the shipyard investment brief to the MoCIIP industrial desk for pre-authorization before resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of the Memorandum of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public Office attached to the Primary Court of the relevant Governorate (Ministry of Justice, Sultanate of Oman).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The sole foreign member attends in person or through a notarized and apostilled/consularly legalized power of attorney holder. The MOA is engrossed in Arabic and states the SPC name, issued and subscribed capital, shipbuilding and vessel-repair activities, registered office in Oman, single-member governance, manager appointment and audit framework. The notary verifies legal capacity, witnesses signatures, registers the MOA and retains a certified copy; any power of attorney executed abroad must bear Omani consular legalization.
required_dossiers: Draft MOA in Arabic, with English translation
Passport copies with certified Arabic translation
Power of attorney with apostille or Omani consular legalization
Lease or allocation letter for the future registered office or Madayn industrial plot
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary queries the Arabic translation, the foreign power of attorney or the shareholder's capacity, cure by re-legalization at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and resubmit within 5 working days. Any defect in the capital or activity clause is corrected through a supplementary MOA executed before the same notary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: MoCIIP Commercial Registration Department / Investment Services Center.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarized MOA and ancillary declarations through the Invest Oman portal. The registry validates the SPC entity type, approved name, activity scope and sole-shareholding structure; pay the statutory commercial registration fee and publication fee; upon approval MoCIIP issues a provisional certificate of incorporation and CR number and forwards the extract for Official Gazette publication.
required_dossiers: Notarized Memorandum of Association
Name reservation confirmation
Office lease or registered-address title documents
Shareholder declaration on capital remittance plan
Executed power of attorney and AML clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry flags inconsistent activity classification, amend the MOA by a resolution of the single member and re-file the activity clause. If the application is suspended for sanctions review, provide CBO watchlist clearance and ROP police clearance; a non-approval may be appealed to the MoCIIP Undersecretary within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Register issuance, Gazette publication and capital deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: MoCIIP Commercial Registration Department; Central Bank of Oman (CBO) licensed retail bank.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After CR approval, confirm payment of the Official Gazette publication fee so the registry publishes the company extract; collect the CR extract and digital company seal. Open the corporate bank account at a CBO-licensed bank by presenting the CR, MOA and board/single-member resolution; wire the subscribed paid-up capital from the sole member's offshore account and obtain an account balance certificate recording the capital-deposit.
required_dossiers: Provisional certificate of incorporation
Notarized MOA and CR extract
Resolution appointing bank signatories
Passport copies of managers and authorized signatories
Utility bill or lease proving the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests economic-substance or source-of-funds evidence, provide the shipyard business plan, customer LC/escrow schedule and audited financial statements of the parent. If Official Gazette publication is delayed, request expedition from the Ministry of Legal Affairs; any CR data error is corrected by an administrative rectification request.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: OCCI registration and industrial estate plot allocation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Oman Chamber of Commerce and Industry (OCCI); Public Establishment for Industrial Estates (Madayn).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company as an OCCI member under the shipbuilding/maritime industrial category and pay the annual subscription. Submit to Madayn an industrial plot application for a shipyard site, including the proposed dry dock, berth, fabrication and painting workshop layout. Madayn issues the plot allotment letter and site development guidelines, which form the basis for environmental and civil-defense review.
required_dossiers: CR extract and notarized MOA
OCCI membership application form
Madayn industrial plot application and site layout drawings
Capital deposit certificate and financial capacity statement
Preliminary Environment Authority no-objection letter for the site
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Madayn has no immediate plot, negotiate a temporary provisional site within an existing shipyard lease while the plot allotment is processed. If OCCI queries the membership category, obtain MoCIIP's ISIC confirmation letter and re-file. Plot allocation disputes are handled through Madayn administrative objection procedures.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: MoCIIP Directorate General of Industries, Industrial Licensing Department, through the Invest Oman industrial window.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the industrial operating license application with the Madayn plot lease, proposed annual shipbuilding and vessel-repair capacity, machinery and equipment list, manning plan and notarized MOA. Attach the prior Environmental Authority consent and ROP Civil Defense NOC; pay the industrial license fee. The license fixes the operational scope as construction and repair of deep-sea dry-cargo and container vessels under ISIC 3011.
required_dossiers: CR extract and notarized MOA
Madayn plot lease or allocation letter
Environmental Authority environmental clearance or NOC
ROP Civil Defense fire-safety NOC
Machinery list and shipyard layout drawings
Capital deposit certificate and financial feasibility statement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the licensing desk questions foreign-ownership eligibility, present the MoCIIP confirmation that commercial shipbuilding is not on the FDI negative list. If capacity or technology documentation is insufficient, submit the shipyard master plan, equipment purchase pro-forma invoices and technical partner agreements; any refusal may be cured by supplementation and appeal to the MoCIIP Minister within 60 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Environmental approval and civil defense / occupational clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Environment Authority of Oman (EA), EIA Department; Royal Oman Police (ROP), Directorate General of Civil Defense; Ministry of Labour, Occupational Safety and Health Inspectorate.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Category-A Environmental and Social Impact Assessment and Environmental Management Plan for the shipyard covering dredging, dry-dock construction, steel fabrication, coating and painting emissions, hazardous waste streams and marine discharge. After EA approval, obtain the ROP Civil Defense fire-safety design certification for workshops, paint stores and utilities, and the structural load inspection of dry-dock walls, gantry cranes and fabrication bays by accredited engineers. Secure the Ministry of Labour OSH workplace clearance before commissioning.
required_dossiers: ESIA report and environmental management plan
Marine water-quality and ballast-water management plan
VOC and hazardous air pollutant emission inventory with abatement design
ROP Civil Defense fire-safety design dossier compliant with Omani Fire Code and NFPA standards
Structural load certificates for dry dock, gantry cranes and fabrication bays
OSH policy, risk assessment, confined-space and hot-work permit system
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If EA requires additional marine-baseline surveys, engage an EA-approved environmental consultancy, supplement the EIA and resubmit within the statutory response window. If Civil Defense rejects the welding or painting bay layout, implement additional fire-suppression and compartmentation upgrades and resubmit within 20 days. OSH enforcement notices are cured by a corrective action plan submitted to the Labour inspector.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: MoCIIP Directorate General of Industries, Industrial Licensing Department, acting with Madayn (Public Establishment for Industrial Estates) for site allocation and with the Environment Authority and ROP Civil Defense as statutory consents authorities.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Industrial Operating Permit (Rukhsah Sina'iyah) for commercial shipbuilding and vessel repair, issued under the Omani Law for the Regulation of Industry and its implementing ministerial decisions, with licensed scope referencing ISIC 3011 / NAICS 336611.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environment Authority (EA) of the Sultanate of Oman, Environmental Assessment and Permitting Directorate.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category A — Full Environmental and Social Impact Assessment (ESIA) required, as the proposed dry dock, dredging, steel fabrication, surface preparation and painting operations, VOC emissions and hazardous waste streams bring the project within the EA high-impact classification; EA consent is integrated as a mandatory NOC in the industrial licensing chain.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with the Omani ambient air, wastewater reuse and marine discharge standards set by EA: no untreated process effluent to marine waters; treated effluent criteria generally within pH 6-9, COD up to 75-150 mg/L site-specific, no detectable organotin compounds; VOC capture from paint and coating booths of at least 85-90% or equivalent abatement; suspended solids from dry-dock works contained by silt curtains and sediment controls; hazardous wastes including spent abrasive, paint residues and waste oils must be segregated, manifested and routed to EA-licensed treatment and disposal operators, with separate marine outfall and stormwater permits obtained as applicable.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate from the ROP Directorate General of Civil Defense for workshops, paint and chemical stores, dry-dock utilities and site accommodation, assessed against the Omani Fire Code and NFPA 101 / NFPA 30 requirements for welding, painting and fuel storage; structural integrity and load certification by licensed engineers for dry-dock walls, gantry cranes and fabrication bays; Ministry of Labour Occupational Safety and Health workplace clearance covering confined spaces, hot work, working at height, noise and hazardous-substance controls; berth and seaward waterfront construction additionally requires the approval of the competent maritime/transport authority for the Sultanate's coastline.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: General Authority for Taxation (GAT) of the Sultanate of Oman (الهيئة العامة للضرائب); e-portal: https://taxoman.gov.om. Customs clearance functions are administered through the national 'Bayane' (Bayān) single window operated by Oman Customs within the Tax Authority portfolio.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) Incorporate the Single Person Company (SPC) before the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Investment Promotion (MOCIIP) and obtain the Commercial Registration (CR) certificate. 2) The Tax Authority automatically issues the corporate Tax Identification Number (TIN) upon CR data exchange; the SPC must activate its profile on the Taxoman portal and obtain the official Tax Card (al-Bitaaqah ad-Dareebiyyah). 3) File mandatory VAT registration within 30 days after taxable turnover exceeds OMR 38,500, or elect voluntary registration once turnover exceeds OMR 19,250, both via the Taxoman e-services portal. 4) Obtain the customs registration code in the Bayane single-window before the first export shipment. 5) Register as an employer for social security purposes where applicable; no separate municipal trade tax registration is required for shipyard activities.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Oman has no US-style check-the-box regime and no hybrid mismatch elections. Available statutory elections: (i) VAT tax-group (fiscal unity) election for related persons satisfying the common financial, economic and organizational control test; (ii) voluntary VAT registration election below the mandatory threshold; (iii) election to apply zero rating to export supplies supported by statutory export evidence; (iv) joint arrangements may elect separate segment registration under the Tax Authority's discretionary case law; the SPC itself is a juridical taxable person and cannot elect pass-through treatment.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under the GCC Unified VAT Agreement and Oman VAT Law (Royal Decree No. 121/2020), effective 16 April 2021
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Mandatory registration: OMR 38,500 annual taxable turnover; voluntary registration: OMR 19,250 annual taxable turnover; registration application must be submitted on the Taxoman portal within 30 days of crossing the mandatory threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time central fiscal clearance, API connectivity mandate, or digital stamping regime is currently operational in Oman. The Tax Authority has announced a phased national e-invoicing mandate adopting PEPPOL standards, expected to commence with B2G and large B2B sectors. Until activation, the SPC must issue compliant tax invoices containing all statutory fields under Article 48 of the VAT Law and preserve electronic or paper originals for the statutory five-year retention window; VAT return filing on the Taxoman portal is mandatory.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero rating applies to the export of an ocean container vessel where the SPC supplies the vessel to a non-resident customer and the vessel is physically removed from Omani/GCC territory within 90 days of supply (or within a period approved by GAT), supported by conclusive proof of export, including the customs export declaration, voyage documentation, port clearance and shipping documents. Ship repair and refit services performed on vessels engaged in international transport are zero-rated as services directly connected to international transportation, provided the customer is non-resident and the contract supports the international voyage. Ship stores, bunker fuel and spare parts supplied for international voyages may also be zero-rated if separately contracted and evidenced.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Bayane single-window final acceptance)
Bill of Lading or Sea Waybill evidencing loading at an Omani port
Commercial Invoice referencing the vessel sale and zero-rated supply
Inward Remittance Certificate from an Omani-licensed bank evidencing receipt of export proceeds
Vessel Delivery and Acceptance Protocol signed by master, shipyard and buyer
Port Clearance / departure certificate and AIS track record evidencing departure from Omani territorial waters
Customs valuation and any export permit documentation for dual-use or ship-related materials
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: GAT may retrospectively revoke zero rating and assess 5% VAT plus interest where export documentation is deficient, the vessel does not leave Omani territory within the prescribed period, or the supply is recharacterized as a domestic supply. Fraudulent zero-rating claims constitute tax evasion: the statutory penalty is 100% of the evaded tax, escalable to 200% on repeat offences, with potential criminal prosecution, director disqualification, asset freeze and publication of judgments. All export records must be retained for five years. For related-party export sales, transfer-pricing adjustments may additionally trigger corporate income tax reassessment, 1% monthly delay interest and underlying penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Oman (CBO) — the sole regulatory authority for monetary policy, banking licensing, foreign exchange operations, and payment and settlement systems within the Sultanate of Oman.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Omani Rial (OMR) is fully convertible for both current and capital account transactions, pegged to the USD at a mid-rate of 1 OMR ≈ 2.6008 USD. Oman does not maintain exchange controls restricting profit remittance, dividend distribution, or capital repatriation for foreign investors. Current account payments require only standard commercial documentation; capital account movements are subject to reporting to the CBO and applicable taxation (e.g., corporate tax clearance through the Oman Tax Authority). No general pre-approval is required for remittance of profits, but the underlying activity must be compliant with Anti-Money Laundering (AML) and Counter-Financing of Terrorism (CFT) regulations, and the bank must be satisfied as to the source of funds and purpose of payment.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Oman imposes no statutory export proceeds surrender or mandatory conversion requirement. Exporters may maintain foreign currency receipts in authorised bank accounts in Oman or abroad. There is no prescribed timeline for conversion. However, banks are required to ensure that all export documentation (e.g., shipping bills, invoices, customs declarations) is consistent and that transfers are supported by valid trade contracts to mitigate trade-based money laundering risks.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low — Offshore electronic money institutions (EMIs) and digital-only payment service providers are not recognised in Oman. Any entity performing cross-border payment services, wallet issuance, or money transmission must hold a CBO licence or operate through a licenced exchange house. Unlicenced foreign EMIs cannot legally offer services to Omani-resident entities or manage transactions in OMR. Therefore, risk management must rely on conventional correspondent banking and trade finance rails.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Mandatory for newly formed SPCs. CBO and the Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) require that at least one director, the beneficial owner, and all authorised signatories attend an in-person KYC interview at the bank’s premises in Oman. Remote/electronic account opening is only permitted for existing banking relationships or for accounts with negligible risk. For a foreign-owned shipping construction company, physical presence is effectively compulsory to satisfy customer due diligence (CDD) and enhanced due diligence (EDD) obligations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) opaque ownership structure — foreign situs holding or nominees.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full UBO register with direct and indirect ownership percentages, source-of-wealth documentation, CVs of directors, org chart, certified copy of the commercial register, memorandum and articles of association, and a legal opinion from an Omani licensed law firm confirming the UBO chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Shipbuilding in maritime sector may trigger sanctions/dual-use scrutiny (e.g., ships capable of military or nuclear cargo use).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed commercial contract and classification society documentation, end-user and end-use certification, UN sanctions screening report, and a compliance declaration that the vessel is not for military or prohibited purposes.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdiction flows — payments from or to shipping registries, flag states, or counterparties in high-risk countries.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Evidence of legitimate shipping operations: bills of lading, charter parties, port call logs, vessel registration papers, and enhanced counterparty due diligence on all trade partners.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party payments or payables to related foreign entities with unclear commercial basis.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Intercompany agreements, pricing policies, transfer pricing documentation, invoices with full descriptions, and a notarised explanation of the commercial rationale.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant wire transfer protocols: (i) Capital injection must be made to a dedicated Capital Escrow/Investment Account in Oman via SWIFT MT103; (ii) The remitter must be the foreign shareholder or an identified lender; (iii) The purpose code on the SWIFT message must correspond to the Omani Foreign Direct Investment classification (or the bank’s internal code for capital subscription), accompanied by a Share Capital Pledge / Board Resolution and proof of share allotment; (iv) The Oman Commercial Registration and Foreign Investment Licence (from MOCIIP) must be presented to the receiving bank; (v) All amounts must be received in OMR or convertible foreign currency; the bank will verify the transaction against the Central Bank’s Foreign Exchange and AML/CFT underwriting guidelines.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for trade settlements: (i) Direct supplier payments via SWIFT MT103 (customer credit transfer); (ii) Documentary letters of credit issued by the Omani bank via SWIFT MT700 and amended via MT707, typically used for the import of steel plates, machinery, marine equipment; (iii) Standby LCs or demand guarantees (SWIFT MT760) to support shipbuilding performance obligations; (iv) Coupon / instalment payments under a maritime instalment LC structure require presentation of shipbuilder’s progress certificates and invoices; (v) All outbound payments must be supported by underlying trade invoices, proof of customs clearance, and alignment with the payment schedule.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Currency Swaps (for major counterparties with CBO approval)
Currency Options (only for hedging of genuine commercial exposure)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Investment Promotion (MCIIP) – Commercial Registry via the Invest Easy Portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary rule: filing must be completed not later than the last day of the month of the CR issuance anniversary; a grace period of 30 calendar days is allowed after that date in practice.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of OMR 100 (approx. USD 260) plus one-month suspension warnings; failure to renew and cure within 90 days triggers administrative strike-off of the SPC from the Commercial Register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return and Audited Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Fiscal year end is normally 31 December; the return and audited financial statements must be filed within four months after the fiscal year end (by 30 April) with a permissible extension to 30 June for filings submitted through a licensed tax agent.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monthly late-filing penalty of 5% of the tax liability, accrued with a statutory maximum cap; non-filing after the extension triggers an additional OMR 400 (USD 1,039) administrative fine and potential criminal liability against the director.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value Added Tax (VAT) Periodic Return and Payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Quarterly filing and payment due by the last day of the first month following the end of each VAT tax period, e.g., Q1 (January–March) due 30 April.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A monthly late-payment penalty of 1% of unpaid VAT; serious and continued non-compliance leads to collection orders, VAT deregistration, and suspension of import/export activities of the shipyard.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Municipal Business License Renewal (for Shipyard Industrial Premises)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local Municipality – Muscat Municipality Licensing Department / Aman System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Calendar-year deadline: all municipal business licenses expire on 31 December; renewal application must be submitted before that date or within 30 days after to avoid interruption of operations.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal fee of OMR 50 (approx. USD 130) per full month of non-renewal; non-renewal for more than 60 days may result in closure notice and removal of the business license for the shipyard premises.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Statutory independent audit is mandatory for every Omani SPC whose annual gross turnover exceeds OMR 500,000 (approx. USD 1,300,000) or whose total assets exceed OMR 1,000,000 (approx. USD 2,600,000); SPCs operating in commercial shipbuilding are considered medium-risk and are required to prepare audited financial statements for renewal of the maritime construction license regardless of the turnover threshold.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted in Oman; companies below the audit threshold may use Omani GAAP as approved by the MoCIIP, but all foreign-owned SPCs must maintain accounting records under IFRS presentation when filing consolidated or standalone tax returns with the Oman Tax Authority.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Oman’s Beneficial Ownership Regulations, the SPC must maintain an up-to-date register of beneficial owners at its registered office and provide an annual confirmation of that register during the CR renewal process. Any transfer of shares, change of control, or direct-indirect ownership change requires an immediate MCIIP UBO register update within 30 days of the transaction; there is no annual end-of-year-only confirmation option. Failure to confirm the register is a separate registrable default subject to fines of up to OMR 500 (USD 1,299) per default.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 500 – USD 1,200 annually for registered office facility and in-country corporate secretarial support in Muscat
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500 – USD 8,500 depending on the number of shareholding movements, intercompany transactions, and overseas financing structures

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 15% (Royal Decree 50/2022, unified federal income tax law; applicable to the Omani-source and worldwide taxable income of a resident Single Person Company).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualifying strategic industrial projects (including commercial shipbuilding under ISIC 3011) may obtain ministerial income tax holidays of up to 5 years; entities registered in Sohar, Salalah, or Duqm Free Zones benefit from income tax exemptions of up to 30 years; accelerated capital allowances on plant, machinery, and dry-dock infrastructure; reinvestment reserve deductions for industrial expansion.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Omani Corporate Income Tax Return (Form ITC-1) filed via the Oman Tax Authority electronic portal 'Taxy' (www.tax.gov.om); taxpayer registration number (TRN) is mandatory and Qualified Tax Accountants may file under power of attorney.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 5 months after the end of the tax year; calendar-year taxpayers must file by 30 April of the following year unless the Secretariat General for Taxation grants a written extension.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross invoiced revenue from ocean-going container vessel construction, hull fabrication, conversion, and dry-dock repair services; recognize on a percentage-of-completion basis in accordance with the long-term contract rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident shipbuilder with no Oman permanent establishment (PE) must report only Omani-source contract revenue and may exclude foreign fabrication income; treaty PE thresholds apply.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Steel plate and marine materials, propulsion systems, outsourced block fabrication, subcontract dry-dock labour, consumable tools, and direct production overheads attributable to vessel construction contracts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct only costs economically connected to the Omani-source contract revenue; allocable home-office costs require contemporaneous supporting allocation schedules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Box 1 less Box 2; must reconcile to audited shipyard financial statements; contract retentions are taxable when billed unless the percentage-of-completion method is approved.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Gross profit apportionment for a non-resident contractor must reflect step-by-step PE activity in Oman; mere procurement outside Oman is not attributable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Management and administrative expenses, engineering and design fees paid to third parties, port and harbour charges, insurance, and finance costs on shipping and yard equipment; subject to the arm's-length and beneficial-ownership rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border charges to parent or affiliates are deductible only with valid contracts, TRC of the payee, and proof of actual services rendered; otherwise 10% withholding applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax-computed depreciation on graving docks, ship lifts, gantry cranes, CNC cutting machinery, and yard buildings; the tax depreciation schedule under RD 50/2022 differs from accounting depreciation and must be reconciled.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident entities must maintain a separate fixed-asset register for Oman PE assets; imported assets must be recorded at customs-cleared cost in OMR.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add back: general provisions and contingent liabilities, fines and criminal penalties, unlicensed donations, CEO excess remuneration, and any transfer-pricing adjustment disallowed by the Oman Tax Authority.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident head-office general overhead not directly attributable to Oman operations is a non-deductible add-back unless an OECD-compliant allocation method is documented.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 – Taxable Income Before Loss Set-Off
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable profit after add-backs and deductions; the figure must agree with the audited financial statements submitted with the return.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident taxpayers compute this line only after applying the relevant treaty rate and/or permanent establishment attribution rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax losses of the preceding maximum of 5 years, subject to continuity of ownership and business activity tests; set-off against Box 7 taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident's Oman PE losses are ring-fenced to the Oman PE and cannot be surrendered to or from the foreign head office.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Applicable tax at the 15% statutory corporate rate on Box 7 after Box 8; free-zone and tax-holiday sectors enter the applicable 0% amount.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The non-resident computes tax on Omani-source income at the 15% statutory rate unless a Double Taxation Agreement prescribes a lower rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 10 – Advance Payments and Foreign Tax Credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits for quarterly corporate income tax instalments, any tax deducted at source in Oman, and foreign tax credits on treaty-qualified foreign income; supporting certificates must be attached.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents attach the foreign tax credit schedule and TRC to verify credit eligibility; excess credit may be carried forward but not refunded.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Box 9 less Box 10; if positive, payment must be settled before or on the statutory deadline; if negative, a refund claim is subject to desktop audit and offset against outstanding liabilities.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any refund to a non-resident is remitted only after verification of the Oman bank account and settlement of all outstanding Oman tax and customs liabilities.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of OMR 100 per month, up to a maximum of OMR 1,000 per return; late payment surcharge of 1% per month (12% per annum) on the unpaid tax; negligent misdeclaration penalty of 50% of the additional tax; wilful evasion attracts criminal fines up to OMR 50,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years; auditors and tax agents are jointly liable where they knowingly assist in defective filings.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% (Oman does not impose dividend withholding tax; dividends paid by the SPC to a foreign parent shareholder are distributed gross and are not subject to Omani tax).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim reduced or nil treaty rates: obtain a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the shareholder's foreign tax authority; upload the TRC and the OTA treaty-relief application via the Taxy portal before the distribution or payment date; provide declaration of beneficial ownership and proof of economic substance; retain underlying loan, royalty, and service contracts for audit. The Oman Tax Authority may issue a certificate confirming the applicable treaty treatment; any over-withheld amount is recoverable by objection within the statutory limits.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: IP royalties and technical ship-design fees to non-residents: statutory withholding 10%, generally treaty-reduced to 5–10%; interest on parent or third-party vessel-financing debt: statutory withholding 10%, treaty-reduced typically to 5–10% (financial institutions) or 0–10% (other lenders); management and technical service fees for services performed in Oman: 10%; no WHT on dividends or capital gains.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: OMR 1.5 million aggregate annual related-party transactions or OMR 10 million total business revenue triggers the mandatory Local File and Master File requirement under the Oman Tax Authority Transfer Pricing Guidelines (RD 50/2022); Country-by-Country Report notification applies to MNE groups with consolidated group revenue above OMR 200 million (OECD-aligned).
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Oman does not operate a separate UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) regime; however, RD 50/2022 codifies a general anti-avoidance rule (GAAR) and CFC rules requiring the SPC to evidence genuine commercial activity in Oman. For a shipyard SPC, substance is proven by physical dry-dock and fabrication premises, local engineering and project-management staff, Omani board decision-making, steel procurement control, and retention of design/production IP risks. Absent substance, the Oman Tax Authority may recharacterize transactions, deny free-zone or treaty benefits, and attribute passive income.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Understating container-vessel contract revenue through side agreements, issuing false invoices for steel and marine equipment, inflating dry-dock labour costs, cash-skimming from repair and conversion payments, or deliberately omitting offshore fabrication income from the ITC-1 return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine of OMR 5,000 to OMR 50,000 and/or imprisonment up to 5 years; additional tax at 15% on the unreported income plus a 1% monthly late-payment surcharge; seizure of yard assets and freezing of bank accounts; publication of the conviction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil is pierced where directors, the SPC manager, or the beneficial owner sign or authorize false returns; personal joint and several liability for unpaid tax, fines and civil restitution arises; courts may issue travel bans, freeze personal assets, bar the individuals from managing any Omani company for up to 10 years, and impose custodial sentences.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying group service charges with no verifiable service, interest-free or inflated intercompany loans from the foreign parent, excessive royalties on ship-design IP, or failing to prepare contemporaneous Local File / Master File documentation for related-party transactions above the OMR threshold.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization of the Omani taxpayer's income at arm's length; disallowance of inflated deductions; additional corporate tax at 15% on the upward adjustment; monthly interest of 1% on the deficiency; administrative penalty for missing TP documentation up to OMR 5,000 per file and up to 50% of the adjusted additional tax for gross negligence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the tax compliance officer are personally accountable for maintaining and certifying TP documentation; knowing cooperation with a sham TP arrangement exposes directors to personal fines and disqualification orders; the Oman Tax Authority may pursue restitution from individuals who signed the false intercompany contracts.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance / Treaty Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the SPC solely as a conduit to hold shipbuilding contracts and divert profits offshore, with no local dry-dock operations, no Omani payroll, no board meeting in Oman, and no steel or logistics procurement control; artificial structuring to claim free-zone tax exemption or treaty benefits without underlying business activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR application results in recharacterization of the arrangement, cancellation of the free-zone income tax exemption, denial of treaty relief, retroactive assessment of tax at 15% on all profits, and penalties for non-disclosure; the Omani Commercial Companies Law permits forced dissolution of shell companies.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominee directors and the beneficial owner face personal liability for misrepresentation to the Oman Tax Authority and the Commercial Register; civil restitution of all unpaid taxes and penalties; travel bans and asset freezes where funds were extracted as hidden distributions; criminal conviction for fraud where shell documentation was used to deceive creditors or tax authorities.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Sanctions Evasion in Maritime Payments
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Structuring shipyard payment flows through maritime installment letters of credit or escrow accounts to conceal trades with sanctioned end-users, accepting cash or bearer instruments for vessel repairs, false invoicing of block fabrication through shell suppliers, or failure to file Suspicious Transaction Reports (STRs) on unusual maritime financing arrangements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Oman AML Law (Royal Decree 30/2016 as amended): imprisonment up to 15 years and fines up to OMR 300,000; confiscation of the vessel, equipment, escrow balances, and shipyard property; cancellation of the maritime license; prohibition from participating in public tenders; enhanced Central Bank and Oman Tax Authority cross-reporting of the SPC.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, the AML Compliance Officer, and the MLRO are criminally liable for wilful or reckless failure to apply customer due diligence on foreign shipowners and for omitting STRs; personal fines and imprisonment may be imposed independently of corporate sanctions; courts may order personal confiscation of illicit gains and a lifelong bar from the maritime finance sector.
